title: U.S. House · New Jersey's 9th District
area: Northern New Jersey, including all or part of Bergen, Hudson, and Passaic counties, including Paterson and Clifton.

context.text: Incumbent Nellie Pou won the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary unopposed. Rosemary Pino won a contested Republican primary, defeating Tiffany Burress 51.3%-48.7%.

Ballotpedia identifies NJ-9 as a 2026 battleground race. Citing New Jersey Monitor reporting, Ballotpedia notes the district has historically been safe Democratic ground but grew more Republican after 2021 redistricting; Pou's 4.9-point win in 2024 was the narrowest this millennium, and Donald Trump narrowly carried the district that year. As of August 2026, major forecasters rated the race Likely Democratic or Leans Democratic.
As of June 30, 2026, Pou had raised $2.66 million in campaign funds and Pino had raised $438,000.

summary.text: Nellie Pou is the Democratic incumbent for New Jersey's 9th Congressional District, elected in 2024 to succeed the late Rep. Bill Pascrell and sworn in on January 3, 2025. She spent decades in Paterson city government and then served 14 years in the New Jersey General Assembly and 13 years in the New Jersey Senate before running for Congress. She serves on the House Committee on Homeland Security and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure, and is seeking a second term.

background.text: Born in Paterson, New Jersey, on May 20, 1956.
Studied at Kean College, Rutgers University, and the University of Virginia.

Worked for the City of Paterson for more than 40 years, according to her official biography, including as Director of Human Resources and as Business Administrator. Ballotpedia lists her as chair of the city's Department of Human Resources from 1983 to 1997.

Served on the New Jersey Task Force on Child Abuse and Neglect and the Passaic County Planning and Policy Partnership Committee, and on state commissions including the New Jersey Complete Count Commission for the 2020 Census and the New Jersey Criminal Sentencing and Disposition Commission.

Entered the New Jersey General Assembly in 1997 as the first woman and first Latina to represent the 35th District; chaired the Assembly Appropriations Committee and served as Deputy Speaker. She served 14 years in the Assembly.
First elected to the New Jersey Senate in 2011 and re-elected in 2013, 2017, 2021, and 2023; served 13 years, including as Senate Majority Caucus Chair and Chair of the Senate Commerce Committee.
Chaired the New Jersey Legislative Latino Caucus and was the first New Jersey legislator to serve as President of the National Hispanic Caucus of State Legislators.
Was selected in August 2024 to replace Rep. Bill Pascrell on the Democratic ballot after his death, and won the November 2024 general election 50.8% to 45.9%.

Sworn into the U.S. House on January 3, 2025, as the first Latina from New Jersey in Congress. Serves on the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee (Vice Ranking Member of its Aviation Subcommittee) and the Homeland Security Committee.
Received an honorary doctorate from William Paterson University in May 2024 and was named to InsiderNJ's list of New Jersey's 100 Policymakers in 2020.

priorities.text: Campaign website says she has been "committed to improving the lives of New Jerseyans," citing better schools, more affordable healthcare, and criminal-justice reform as career priorities.
priorities.quote: From fighting for better schools for our kids to more affordable health care, to criminal justice reform – Nellie has been at the forefront of some of New Jersey's and America's toughest fights.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Homeland Security (Subcommittee on Counterterrorism and Intelligence) and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure (Aviation; Highways and Transit; Water Resources and Environment subcommittees).
Announced $3 million in federal funding her office says it helped secure for road-safety improvements to Passaic Avenue in Kearny, including upgraded pedestrian crossings and traffic signalization.

candidates.name: Rosemary Pino
candidates.ballotNote: Won a contested June 2, 2026 Republican primary, defeating Tiffany Burress 51.3%-48.7%.

summary.text: Rosemary "Rosie" Pino is the Republican nominee for New Jersey's 9th Congressional District. A Rutgers finance graduate who worked in county government and the U.S. Treasury Department, she served on the Clifton Board of Education and has served on the Clifton City Council since 2019. She won the June 2026 Republican primary over Tiffany Burress, 51.3% to 48.7%, and describes herself as having left the Democratic Party to run on a working-class platform.

background.text: According to her campaign website, born to blue-collar immigrant parents from Ecuador and raised in New Jersey by a single mother; she has lived in Clifton for over 30 years. She attended Clifton High School.
Describes herself as a teen mother and high school dropout who earned a GED and then a bachelor's degree in finance from Rutgers University while working multiple jobs.

Began her career in the Passaic County Community College finance department, then joined Passaic County One Stop, a career-development center that teaches résumé and interview skills to unemployed residents. Her campaign website also says she worked as a bank examiner at the U.S. Department of the Treasury.
Ran unsuccessfully for the Clifton school board in 2011, finishing fifth.
Served two terms on the Clifton Board of Education; Ballotpedia lists her service as 2014 to 2019.
Elected to the Clifton City Council in 2018 and has served since 2019; her campaign website says she was the first minority member elected to the council.
According to her campaign website, she left the Democratic Party and became a Republican.

Her campaign website says she founded multiple nonprofits, volunteers with Relay for Life, serves on the board of the Theater League of Clifton, and is a PTO president. It says she lives in Clifton with her husband Eric and their 11 children, two of them adopted from foster care.
Won the June 2, 2026 Republican primary over Tiffany Burress, 51.3% to 48.7%.

priorities.text: Campaign website says that on the Clifton Board of Education she "fought tirelessly to ensure the city provided students with a top-notch education while maintaining fiscal responsibility," citing more than $8 million invested in capital improvements and more than $3 million allocated for children's safety.
priorities.quote: Rosie fought tirelessly to ensure the city provided students with a top-notch education while maintaining fiscal responsibility.

record.text: Has served on the Clifton City Council since 2019.
Served on the Clifton Board of Education from 2014 to 2019.

candidates.name: Terrisa Bukovinac

summary.text: Terrisa Bukovinac is an anti-abortion activist running in New Jersey's 9th Congressional District on the "Save Our Babies" ballot line. She describes herself as a "progressive pro-life atheist" and previously led Democrats for Life of America and ran in New Jersey's 2024 Democratic presidential primary.

background.text: Born April 4, 1981.
Founded Pro-Life San Francisco in 2017, became president of Democrats for Life of America in 2020, and founded Progressive Anti-Abortion Uprising in 2021.
Ran for the 2024 Democratic presidential nomination; the New Jersey Globe reports hers was the only name besides Joe Biden on New Jersey's 2024 Democratic presidential primary ballot.

Filed for the 9th District in June 2026 with the slogan "Save Our Babies". Her petition lists an address in Ellendale, Tennessee, and the New Jersey Globe noted she has no obvious connections to New Jersey.

candidates.researchNotes: No detailed campaign website content, Candidate Connection survey response, or public statements specific to this race were found for Terrisa Bukovinac beyond her Ballotpedia listing and ballot line.
